dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An indexed family of five predicates on a measure mu, a real-valued function X, and a real parameter K. It dispatches on the index: D010 selects D013, D007 selects D005, D009 selects D012, D008 selects D011, and D003 selects D004.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the property transferred from an input index i with parameter Ki to an output index j with a comparable parameter Kj.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified i and j choose which two of the five analytic predicates are related.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For K, mu, and X, this says: X is measurable; K is positive; X is integrable with integral zero; and for every real lambda, exp(lambda X) is integrable and its integral is at most exp(K^2 lambda^2).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007

binders: There exists one real constant C, chosen before all probability spaces, functions, indices, and scale parameters.
In each clause, Omega is an arbitrary type with a measurable-space structure, mu is an arbitrary probability measure on Omega, and X : Omega -> Real is arbitrary.
The indices i and j range over a five-element type of analytic formulations.
Ki is an implicitly quantified positive real input parameter, and Kj is an existentially quantified real output parameter that may depend on Omega, mu, X, i, j, and Ki.
hypotheses: First clause: X is measurable; i and j are both different from the distinguished linear-exponential-moment index D003; Ki > 0; and the i-indexed predicate holds for (mu, X, Ki).
Second clause: X is measurable and integrable, its integral with respect to mu is zero, Ki > 0, and the i-indexed predicate holds for (mu, X, Ki). No index is excluded in this clause.
conclusions: Under the first clause's hypotheses, there exists Kj > 0 with Kj <= C Ki such that the j-indexed predicate holds for (mu, X, Kj).
Under the second clause's hypotheses, there exists Kj > 0 with Kj <= C Ki such that the j-indexed predicate holds for (mu, X, Kj).
The same absolute constant C works simultaneously for every ordered pair of applicable formulations and for every probability space and real-valued function.
mathematical_definitions: The index type has exactly five cases, which can be labeled by their definitions as Tail, Moment, SquareWindow, SquarePoint, and LinearMGF.
Tail(mu,X,K): X is measurable, K > 0, and for every real t >= 0, mu({|X| >= t}), viewed as a real number, is at most 2 exp(-t^2/K^2).
Moment(mu,X,K): X is measurable, K > 0, X is also almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p >= 1 the function |X|^p is integrable and integral(|X|^p) <= (K sqrt(p))^p.
SquareWindow(mu,X,K): X is measurable, K > 0, and for every real lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K, exp(lambda^2 X^2) is integrable and integral(exp(lambda^2 X^2)) <= exp(K^2 lambda^2).
SquarePoint(mu,X,K): X is measurable, K > 0, exp(X^2/K^2) is integrable, and integral(exp(X^2/K^2)) <= 2.
LinearMGF(mu,X,K): X is measurable, K > 0, X is integrable with integral(X) = 0, and for every real lambda, exp(lambda X) is integrable and integral(exp(lambda X)) <= exp(K^2 lambda^2).
D010, D007, D009, D008, and D003 select Tail, Moment, SquareWindow, SquarePoint, and LinearMGF respectively.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C >= 1 such that, on every probability space, any one of the four formulations Tail, Moment, SquareWindow, and SquarePoint with a positive scale Ki can be converted to any other one with some positive scale Kj <= C Ki, provided X is measurable. Moreover, if X is measurable, integrable, and has integral zero, the same conversion statement holds among all five formulations, now including LinearMGF, still with the same universal C. The conversions are asserted for every ordered pair of formulation indices, so within the stated domains they give mutual comparability of admissible scale parameters up to C.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Only real-valued measurable functions on probability spaces are covered.
The first clause excludes the LinearMGF index at both ends; it asserts no uncentered conversion to or from that formulation.
The all-five-formulations clause requires X to be integrable and to have integral exactly zero before any transfer is obtained.
The theorem compares existence of admissible positive parameters. It does not define or compare least possible parameters, and it does not keep the same parameter; it only produces Kj <= C Ki.

Every conversion implication is vacuous for a particular input tuple if its assumed i-indexed predicate does not hold. The universal statement becomes substantive through those tuples for which an input witness Ki exists.
Positivity of K is built into every indexed predicate and is also separately required for Ki and for the produced Kj.
The Moment formulation quantifies over all real p >= 1, not merely integer orders, and bounds the raw p-th moment rather than explicitly stating a p-th-root norm bound.
All moment-generating and exponential-square integrals have explicit integrability requirements; no extended-valued inequality is being used as a substitute for integrability.
No numerical value of C, optimality claim, symmetry at a fixed scale, independence assumption, or additional probabilistic structure is encoded.
ambiguities: The external implementation body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque in the packet, although its type and surrounding structures identify the standard real-valued Bochner integral.
Real exponentiation in the Moment predicate is specifically Real.rpow. Its bases are nonnegative and its exponents satisfy p >= 1, so exceptional negative-base conventions do not intervene.
